newsitem.title: INDIA: India's IPCL to boost ethylene capacity.
newsitem.headline: India's IPCL to boost ethylene capacity.

text.p: State-run Indian Petrochemicals Ltd (IPCL) plans to expand production capacity at its plant in India's western state of Maharashtra by 30 percent by 1997, the federal government said on Tuesday.

IPCL plans to expand the capacity of the gas cracker and linear low density polyethylene and high density polyethylene (LLDPE/HDPE) plants at Nagothane in Maharashtra, the government said in a statement.
IPCL's ethylene capacity is expected to increase to 400,000 tonnes per annum by 1997 from 300,000 tonnes under the expansion plans, the statement said.
The LLDPE/HDPE capacity is also expected to increase to 220,000 tonnes per annum from 160,000 tonnes in the same period, the statement said.

IPCL on Tuesday signed an agreement with the Indian government to rapidly complete work on plants in Gujarat for the manufacture of chlor alkali and VCM/PVC, the statement said. The capacity expansion plans were also covered by the agreement.

As part of economic reforms launched in 1991, the federal government has evolved a system of fixing targets for state-run firms by signing agreements, or Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs), with them, to give managements a measure of autonomy.
